solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: In search of a style, to a certain extent

parts.note: to be after something is to be seeking it
taken as written
a fashion is a style or manner

explanation.surface: Someone hunting for a look of their own, and finding it only partly.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma splits wordplay from definition; the three pieces are simply laid end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes doing something in a rough or limited way, only partly or not very well.

clue.text: Plant life I'd removed from US state

indicators.note: something removed is taken away, so letters are struck out of a longer word

parts.note: the southeastern American state
the contraction written without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: A botanist notes that certain plants have disappeared from an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: Take ID out of FLORIDA and FLORA is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Flora is the collective term for the plants growing in a particular region or period.

clue.text: Sovereign setting up theatre in Italian capital

indicators.note: in a down clue, setting something up raises it, so the letters read upward, bottom to top
one thing sitting inside another means its letters go within the other's

parts.note: the capital city of Italy
rep, short for repertory, is a kind of theatre company

explanation.surface: A monarch establishing a playhouse in Rome, like an ancient Caesar.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'setting up' reverses everything built before it, so the insertion happens first and the whole result is then read bottom to top. Rep is short for repertory theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor is a supreme ruler of an empire, so a sovereign in the fullest sense.

clue.text: Broadcast melody

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to put a programme out on radio or television

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a tune played on the radio, but the two words are separate meanings; 'Broadcast' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: The word serves as a verb for transmitting a programme and as a noun for a simple tune or song.

clue.text: Material for statue obtainable from sale at bar

indicators.note: what is obtainable from something can be made out of it, so the letters are reworked into something new

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A sculptor buying stone for a statue at a pub auction.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests buying something at a sale, but the three words are raw letters to be mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabaster is a smooth white mineral traditionally carved into statues, vases and ornaments.

clue.text: Alluring woman I found after some time

indicators.note: placed after means the one piece follows the other in the answer

parts.note: an hour is a period of time
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man spots a beautiful woman after waiting a while.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists I first, but 'found after' puts it at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A houri is a beautiful maiden of the Islamic paradise, and by extension any voluptuous, seductive woman.

clue.text: Stuff oneself before boarding old vessel

parts.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old

indicators.note: someone boarding a ship goes inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a vat is a large tank or container
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A passenger gorging on food before getting on an old ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' looks like a time word in the surface, and 'vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a tank here. Ere is the poetic word crosswords love for before.
explanation.definitionFit: To stuff oneself is to eat far too much, which is exactly what overeating means.

clue.text: Police officer, one who manages to bear pressure

indicators.note: to bear is to carry, so one piece holds another inside it

parts.note: a coper is someone who copes
P is the symbol for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: A police officer described as someone who copes well under stress.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a compliment to a stressed officer; in fact 'manages' gives COPER, which holds P.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper is informal British slang for a policeman, just as cop is elsewhere.

clue.text: Charm a Greek character hired out

parts.note: taken as written
mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet
to let a property is to rent it out

explanation.surface: A charming Greek man who works for hire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charm' looks like a verb or a quality; it is the noun, a lucky object. 'Greek character' is a letter of the alphabet, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: An amulet is a small object worn as a lucky charm to ward off evil or bring protection.

clue.text: Sea-fog initially hated at all resorts

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of each following word counts

parts.note: the opening letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers everywhere loathe the cold mist rolling in off the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: A haar is a cold sea mist that drifts in on the east coasts of Scotland and northern England, which is why seaside resorts hate it.
explanation.definitionFit: Haar is the regional name for a chilly mist or fog blowing inland from the North Sea.

clue.text: Person who's tested an explosive device in river?

indicators.note: something in something else sits within it, so one set of letters goes inside another

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, in southwest England
the indefinite article, shortened
a mine is a buried or floating bomb

explanation.surface: Someone who has checked a bomb sitting in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tested' reads as something the person did to the device, but 'Person who's tested' is the definition. The Exe is a favourite crossword river.
explanation.definitionFit: An examinee is the candidate sitting an exam, somebody whose knowledge is being assessed.

clue.text: Basic team Ellen assembled

indicators.note: assembling means putting parts together in a new form, so the letters are rebuilt in another order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A simple side that someone called Ellen has put together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Basic' sits at the front as the definition; the rest is letters to mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemental means fundamental or essential, relating to the first principles of something.

clue.text: Twilled fabric used in looser gear

indicators.note: something used in a thing is contained within it, so the letters run inside the words that follow

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A tough woven cloth used for making baggy clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the gap between the two words at the end of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Serge is a hard-wearing woollen cloth woven with diagonal ribs, used for suits and uniforms.

clue.text: Flat in south, not among the first six

indicators.note: one thing in another sits within it, so these letters go inside the other piece

parts.note: STH is a common abbreviation for south
a flat, level surface is even

explanation.surface: An apartment in the south of the country, excluded from a top-six ranking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' looks like a home; it is the adjective meaning level. South is abbreviated to STH here, not just S.
explanation.definitionFit: The playful definition describes the position right after sixth place, which is being the next one along.

clue.text: Racecourse spy eating river fish

indicators.note: whatever eats something takes it inside, so one piece swallows another

parts.note: a racing tout spies on horses in training and sells tips
R is the standard abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A tipster at the track tucking into a fish caught in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'River fish' looks like the definition, but 'river' is the piece that goes inside and 'fish' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: The trout is a common freshwater game fish of the salmon family.

clue.text: Herb originally only relished, say, by a small number

indicators.note: originally means at the origin or outset, so each word gives up its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letters of the two words
e.g. means for example, as does say
taken as written
No. is the short form of number

explanation.surface: A herb that at first only a few people enjoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Originally' applies to two words, not one. 'Small number' means the abbreviation for number, not a few.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is an aromatic Mediterranean plant whose leaves are used to season cooking, especially pizza.

clue.text: Eavesdrop across in this place, it's reported

parts.note: to go across is to go over

indicators.note: a report is spoken, so the word is taken for how it is said rather than spelt

parts.note: here means in this place

explanation.surface: Listening in on conversations from across the room, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the second piece is swapped for its sound-alike; the first is spelt as it means.
explanation.definitionFit: To eavesdrop is to listen secretly, and to overhear is to catch talk not meant for you.

clue.text: Anchorage in Greek island, by the sound of it

indicators.note: judging by the sound means the spoken form matters, not the spelling

parts.note: Rhodes is a large island in the Dodecanese

explanation.surface: A sheltered harbour on a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anchorage' looks like the Alaskan city; it is a sheltered place where ships anchor, which is the nautical sense of roads, as in Hampton Roads.
explanation.definitionFit: Roads, or a roadstead, is sheltered water near a shore where vessels can ride at anchor, a sailors' term.

clue.text: Attention needed at first to make money

parts.note: to give someone your ear is to pay attention

indicators.note: at first points to the very start, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter only

explanation.surface: Getting rich requires focus from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attention' gives EAR, as in 'lend me your ear'.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn is to receive wages or profit in return for work, bringing income in.

clue.text: Cleric receiving East European magistrate

indicators.note: whatever receives something takes it in, so one letter goes inside another piece

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is the title of a cleric
E is the compass abbreviation
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A clergyman welcoming a judge from Eastern Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East European' reads as one phrase, but it gives two separate letters: one goes inside REV, the other follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was an official in medieval England, such as the chief magistrate of a town or district.

clue.text: Young child in first half of Disney film

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the first half of a word is its opening portion, so only the front letters are kept

parts.note: Fantasia is Disney's 1940 animated film set to classical music

explanation.surface: A little one appearing early in a Disney movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word placing the child, but it is a piece taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: An infant is a baby or very young child, especially one not yet walking or talking.

clue.text: Tradesman swallowing last of coffee in cup

indicators.note: what swallows something takes it inside, so one letter goes within another piece

parts.note: a baker is a tradesman who makes bread

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the final letter only

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper gulping the dregs of his coffee from a mug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cup' is the definition at the end, with 'in' as a link, even though the surface puts the coffee in the cup.
explanation.definitionFit: A beaker is a drinking cup, often tall and without a handle, or a lipped glass container.

clue.text: Move up and down repeatedly — up or down!

indicators.note: in a down clue the word reads the same whether read upward or downward, so it is the same both ways

parts.note: to move up and down, like a cork on water

explanation.surface: An instruction to bounce up and down, whichever way you go.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half repeats the up-and-down image but refers to the letters in the grid, which read the same in either direction.
explanation.definitionFit: To bob is to move quickly and repeatedly up and down, as a float does on water.

clue.text: Railway guard who exposes malpractice?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, literal: a guard signals a train's departure with a whistle
second meaning, figurative: an insider who reports wrongdoing

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the first meaning is taken literally: a British railway guard blows a whistle to send the train off.
explanation.definitionFit: The term describes someone who literally sounds a whistle and, idiomatically, an employee who reports an organisation's wrongdoing to the authorities.
